articles.title: Police advice for Rochdale fans after substance forced Co-op Live evacuation during Don Toliver show
articles.excerpt: Anyone who went to Sunday's Don Toliver concert and has since felt unwell should go to hospital, see their GP or call 101, Greater Manchester Police say.
articles.content_html:
Anyone from the Rochdale borough who was at Don Toliver's Co-op Live concert on Sunday night should seek medical help if they have since felt unwell, police say.

Greater Manchester Police said anyone who has noticed side-effects or become unwell since the event should go to their local hospital, contact their GP or call 101.

Officers were alerted by venue staff shortly after 10pm on Sunday 22 November, after reports that people in the crowd were suffering the effects of a substance released near the end of the show.

Police first said the substance was believed to be tear gas. Later updates described it as unknown, and its identity has not been confirmed.

A major incident was declared and more than 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena on the Etihad Campus in east Manchester.

In an update on Monday evening, GMP said 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure.

One woman was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for assessment and treatment. The other 88 were given dry decontamination at the scene and taken to the Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed.

The major incident was stood down at 4am on Monday. GMP described the incident as isolated, with no wider threat to the public.

Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "We are trying to establish whether any criminality has occurred in relation to this incident."

Police said enquiries were continuing "to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk". Further testing will be carried out on items found at the venue. No arrests have been made.

Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker, Gold Commander on the night, said the priority had been to "ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert".

Co-op Live said it was working closely with GMP to identify the cause, and that the safety and security of visitors was its priority.

Don Toliver ended the Manchester show early. His concert at The O2 in London on Monday 23 November has been rescheduled for 15 December, and Live Nation said tickets will be honoured.

Police have not issued a specific public appeal. Anyone with information can contact GMP on 101 or through LiveChat at gmp.police.uk, or report anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111. In an emergency, call 999.

Sources: Greater Manchester Police statements of 22 and 23 November 2026, as reported by About Manchester, Brit Brief, Examiner Live, IBTimes, Complex and the Associated Press. Image: Greater Manchester Police logo, illustrative.

articles.title: Clover Security Services Ltd to be wound up following resolutions
articles.excerpt: Clover Security Services Ltd, based in Castleton, Rochdale, has passed resolutions for voluntary winding-up at a meeting held on 18 November 2026.
articles.content_html:
Clover Security Services Ltd, based at 32 Chatburn Avenue in Castleton, Rochdale, has passed resolutions to wind up the company voluntarily. The decision was made during a general meeting held on 18 November 2026 at The Waterscape in Leeds.

Tracey Howarth of Aurora Recovery Limited has been appointed as the liquidator for the winding-up process. The company's registered office is located at 42 Leeds and Bradford Road, Kirkstall, Leeds.

The resolutions were passed as both a special and ordinary resolution, allowing for the voluntary winding-up of the company. This process will involve settling any outstanding debts and distributing any remaining assets to creditors.

The closure of Clover Security Services Ltd may impact local employment and service availability in the Castleton area, as the company has been a provider of security services.

articles.title: You may be able to claim for Turner Brothers asbestos
articles.excerpt: Former workers, their families and people who lived near the Spotland factory can still claim, and there are routes for people exposed elsewhere too.
articles.content_html:
People made ill by asbestos from the former Turner Brothers Asbestos factory in Spotland can still claim compensation, 25 years after the company collapsed.

Former workers can claim, and so can people who never worked there, such as relatives exposed to dust on work clothes and people who lived near the factory.

Claims linked to Turner Brothers are handled by the T&N UK Asbestos Trust, which holds a separate fund for Turner Brothers claims. Its website is tandnasbestos.org.uk.

The trust usually pays a set share of a claim's full value rather than the whole amount.

People exposed to asbestos at other workplaces may also be able to claim, even if their employer closed long ago. Mesothelioma, a cancer caused by asbestos, often takes 40 to 50 years to show symptoms.

An employer's insurer is usually responsible even when the firm no longer exists. The Employers' Liability Tracing Office, at elto.org.uk, helps people find a former employer's insurer, though it does not pay compensation itself.

People diagnosed with mesothelioma who cannot trace a liable employer or insurer may be able to claim from the government's Diffuse Mesothelioma Payment Scheme, which pays according to age.

A government lump sum under the Pneumoconiosis etc. (Workers' Compensation) Act 1979 covers certain dust-related diseases when damages cannot be won from an employer, often because it has stopped trading. The claim form helpline is 0800 279 2322.

A separate 2008 mesothelioma scheme covers people exposed through a relative's work clothes, and people who cannot say where they were exposed but were exposed only in the UK.

Since 31 October 2026, dependants claiming under either government scheme after a sufferer died without claiming receive the full amount the sufferer would have been paid.

For a 60-year-old claimant under the 2008 scheme, that raises a dependant's payment from £24,526 to £56,656, according to the government. The change applies to new claims only.

Asbestos products were made at the Spodden Valley site from 1879 until 1998, and it was once the world's largest asbestos textile factory. Turner & Newall went into administration in 2001.

The site's owner, Spodden Park Ltd, began investigation works this month to map where asbestos is buried, ahead of a clean-up and redevelopment.

Compensation claims generally have to begin within three years of diagnosis, or within three years of a death. Some government payments must be claimed within 12 months.

The Greater Manchester Asbestos Victims Support Group, a registered charity, gives free advice on benefits and compensation to people with any asbestos-related disease, and runs support groups for patients and bereaved families.

The group can be contacted on 0161 258 0166, Monday to Friday from 9.30am to 4pm, or at info@gmavsg.org. Specialist asbestos solicitors can advise which routes apply, and many work on a no win, no fee basis.

Sources: T&N Asbestos Trustee Company, GOV.UK, Employers' Liability Tracing Office, Greater Manchester Asbestos Victims Support Group. Photograph: Rochdale Daily.

articles.title: Free health checks in Rochdale identify 1,000 undiagnosed conditions
articles.excerpt: A community health initiative in Rochdale has revealed that half of participants were unaware they needed medical attention, with 1,000 undiagnosed conditions identified.
articles.content_html:
A community initiative offering free health checks across Rochdale, Heywood, and Middleton has identified 1,000 undiagnosed health conditions among participants. Launched on 31 October 2025, the programme has conducted 2,000 health checks, revealing that 50% of those tested were unaware they needed medical attention.

The Community Health Checks programme, commissioned by Rochdale Council and delivered by the Living Well Rochdale Cardiovascular Disease team, aims to improve access to essential health screenings.

Checks are conducted at various locations, including community venues, GP practices, workplaces, and local stores, making it easier for residents to receive health assessments.

Each health check includes blood pressure monitoring, height and weight measurements, and a finger-prick test for blood sugar and cholesterol levels. Participants also receive their Body Mass Index and an assessment to estimate their risk of developing cardiovascular disease over the next decade.

The initiative is designed to help identify potential health concerns early, preventing them from developing into more serious conditions. The Living Well Rochdale CVD team continues to engage with the community to promote health awareness and encourage residents to take advantage of these free services.

articles.title: Rochdale Hornets partner with 10X Athletic for 2027 season
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Hornets have announced a partnership with 10X Athletic, naming them as the official performance nutrition partner for the 2027 season. This collaboration aims to enhance the nutritional support provided to the men's first team, ensuring players are well-prepared for their matches. As part of the partnership, 10X Athletic will supply a range of…
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Hornets have announced a partnership with 10X Athletic, naming them as the official performance nutrition partner for the 2027 season. This collaboration aims to enhance the nutritional support provided to the men's first team, ensuring players are well-prepared for their matches.

As part of the partnership, 10X Athletic will supply a range of supplements, including electrolyte products and protein formulas, specifically designed for athletes. The products are developed with input from various professionals and are third-party tested to meet the standards required for drug-tested athletes.

Danny Lee, head of strength and conditioning for Rochdale Hornets, emphasised the importance of nutrition in players' preparation and recovery. He stated that the partnership will combine the club's environment with 10X Athletic's nutritional expertise, benefiting the players significantly.

Fans of Rochdale Hornets can also benefit from this partnership, as they will have access to a discount code for 10% off 10X Athletic products, allowing them to support the team while enjoying high-quality nutritional supplements.

articles.title: Rochdale Borough Council awards £152,500 contract for Lowerplace Primary School water pipework
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a £152,500 contract for hot and cold water pipework at Lowerplace Primary School to M&R Heating Services Northwest Limited.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has awarded a £152,500 contract for hot and cold water pipework at Lowerplace Primary School to M&R Heating Services Northwest Limited. This contract is part of a two-phase project aimed at upgrading the school's water infrastructure.

The contract was published on the Find a Tender service and is expected to enhance the school's facilities, ensuring better access to water services for the pupils and staff.

This development follows similar contracts awarded for other schools in the borough, including Boarshaw Primary School and Whittaker Moss Primary School, which also received funding for their water pipework upgrades.

The Boarshaw project was awarded to J C Mills & Son Limited for £230,000, while Whittaker Moss's second phase was awarded to W.H. Good Limited for £150,000.

These upgrades are part of Rochdale Borough Council's ongoing commitment to improving educational facilities across the area. The council aims to ensure that all schools meet modern standards for health and safety, particularly in essential services like water supply.

How Lowerplace is affected

  • The £152,500 contract will improve water services at Lowerplace Primary School.
  • Similar contracts have been awarded to other schools in Rochdale for infrastructure improvements.

articles.title: Rochdale White Ribbon vigil: where Wednesday's walk starts and how to join
articles.excerpt: Residents are invited to join a free White Ribbon Day vigil walk and service in Rochdale on Wednesday 25 November 2026, commemorating victims of violence and abuse.
articles.content_html:
Residents are invited to join a free White Ribbon Day vigil walk and service in Rochdale on Wednesday 25 November 2026, commemorating victims of violence and abuse.

The council says the walk begins at 5pm outside Number One Riverside on Smith Street, following introductory speeches. Participants will then walk through the town centre to St Mary in the Baum Parish Church on St Mary's Gate.

A service at the church is scheduled from 6pm until 7pm. The council says everyone is welcome and no booking is needed. Attendees are encouraged to bring LED tealights or candles.

The event is organised by Rochdale Borough Council and partners. The published programme names actor Cait Fitton, actor Callum Lill, activist Gemma Aitchison, White Ribbon ambassador Warren Betts and MP Elsie Blundell among the guest speakers. The council provides community.safety@rochdale.gov.uk for enquiries.

Anyone attending should check the council's listing for any last-minute changes to the arrangements.

Source: https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/events/event/1514/white-ribbon-vigil

articles.title: Middleton Library to explore ghost stories and the real history behind them
articles.excerpt: Middleton Library is hosting a free evening exploring local ghost stories and the historical records behind them on Thursday 26 November 2026.
articles.content_html:
Middleton Library is hosting a free evening exploring local ghost stories and the historical records behind them on Thursday 26 November 2026.

The Haunted Library runs from 4pm to 5.30pm at Middleton Library on Long Street, M24 6DU. The session is intended for adults and teenagers and combines local legends with investigation of photographs, newspaper reports and archival material.

Booking is required by noon on Thursday 26 November, the same day as the event. The council's event listing directs residents to Eventbrite for tickets. People planning to attend should check availability before travelling.

The event offers a chance to separate the stories that have circulated locally from the documented people and events that may have inspired them. The council lists middleton.library@rochdale.gov.uk as the contact for enquiries.

Source: https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/events/event/1499/the-haunted-library---middleton-library

articles.title: Castleton house approved for eight-bed care home
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has approved plans to turn a house on Thornham New Road, Castleton, into a care home for up to eight adults.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has approved plans to turn a house at 9 Thornham New Road, Castleton, into a care home for up to eight adults, with 24-hour care.

The council approved the application on 18 November. The plans include a new upstairs bay window and internal layout changes to the property.

The council received 20 comments on the application. Residents raised concerns about parking, noise and emergency vehicle access to the home.

Highways officers did not object to the application and said the home was unlikely to add much traffic. The driveway has room for three or four cars, and the council requires two parking spaces for a care home of this size.

The applicant says no more than two staff would be on site at once. A planning condition limits the care home to eight residents and requires work to start within three years of approval.

What it means for Castleton

  • The care home is limited to eight residents and must start work within three years of approval.
  • The council requires two parking spaces for a care home of this size, and the driveway has room for three or four cars.

articles.title: Temporary no waiting restriction on part of Lance Corporal Joel Halliwell VC Way in Middleton
articles.excerpt: Drivers face a temporary no waiting restriction on part of Lance Corporal Joel Halliwell VC Way in Middleton from 26 November 2026, according to a council roadworks notice.
articles.content_html:
Drivers using part of Lance Corporal Joel Halliwell VC Way in Middleton face a temporary parking ban from 26 November 2026, according to a Rochdale Borough Council roadworks notice.

The notice, titled Middleton Pantomime, sets out a no waiting restriction at any time along the south westerly side of the road.

It begins 54 metres south east of a point opposite the south easterly kerb line of Old Hall Street and runs for 52 metres in a south easterly direction.

The notice gives no finish date and no reason beyond its title. It includes no diversion details, and no further council statement on the restriction appears in the records available to Rochdale Daily.

Readers can check the notice and a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester on the council website, which also lists other restrictions.

What changes for drivers in Middleton

  • Parking is prohibited at any time along the south westerly side of Lance Corporal Joel Halliwell VC Way from 26 November 2026.
  • The restriction covers a 52-metre stretch beginning 54 metres south east of a point opposite the south easterly kerb line of Old Hall Street.

articles.title: Thinking about fostering? Free advice stall at Rochdale Riverside on Wednesday
articles.excerpt: People considering becoming foster carers can speak to Rochdale Borough Council's fostering team at a free information stall on Wednesday 25 November 2026.
articles.content_html:
People considering becoming foster carers can speak to Rochdale Borough Council's fostering team at a free information stall on Wednesday 25 November 2026.

The drop-in takes place at Rochdale Riverside on Riverside Walk, OL16 1TR, from noon until 2pm. No appointment or booking is required, and the council says the session is open to everyone.

The regular monthly stall is intended for people who want to ask questions before deciding whether to pursue fostering. Visitors can discuss the process directly with council staff rather than committing to an application.

The council lists Fostering@rochdale.gov.uk as the contact address. Residents should consult the official event listing if they need to check the arrangements before travelling.

Source: https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/events/event/1295/fostering-information-session---rochdale-riverside

articles.title: Overwhelming support for veterans' flats plan at Denehurst House
articles.excerpt: Plans for five flats for veterans at Denehurst House have moved closer after a council consultation showed overwhelming support, with Rochdale Council's Cabinet due to decide.
articles.content_html:
Plans to create homes for veterans at Denehurst House have moved a step closer after Rochdale Council said a public consultation showed "overwhelming support" for the proposals.

The historic property is being upgraded to include a public café and five flats for veterans. Concerns about its ownership and legal status prompted the council, which is the legal trustee of Denehurst House and Park, to launch a review and consultation.

A report to the council's Cabinet, which is due to consider the matter tomorrow, says no objections had been received from the public up to the date of the report.

It states: "The consultation showed overwhelming support for use of the property for veterans' accommodation in perpetuity."

If Cabinet approves the proposal, the five flats will be designated as residential accommodation for veterans. The source does not give a timetable for the works beyond the Cabinet decision.
